title: Generalized Abbreviation
summary: Given a string, generate all possible generalized abbreviations by replacing any number of non-overlapping and non-adjacent substrings with their lengths.
statement: Given a string, generate all possible generalized abbreviations by replacing any number of non-overlapping and non-adjacent substrings with their lengths. Ensure no substrings are adjacent or overlap. Include the original string as an abbreviation. Return all valid abbreviations in any order.
constraints: Independently keep or abbreviate each character. Replace every maximal consecutive abbreviated run by its decimal length; do not write adjacent separate counts. Return every result once in any order.
hints: At each position, choose whether to keep the character or add it to an abbreviated run.
Carry an unfinished skip count instead of immediately writing a number for each removed character.
Recurse with skip+1 for abbreviation. To keep a character, flush the skip count, append the character, and reset skip to zero.
At the end flush any remaining count. Binary decisions generate 2^n unique outputs without adjacent abbreviation counts.
editorial: A pending count combines adjacent skipped characters into one legal run. Keeping a letter ends that run and separates it from any later count. Each keep/skip mask corresponds to exactly one output, including the unchanged word and the all-abbreviated length. The oracle scans bit masks and compresses consecutive set-bit positions independently.

tests.explanation: Each of four positions can be kept or abbreviated, giving 16 results. For example w2d replaces or, and 1o1d replaces w and r.
Either keep a or replace its single character by 1, so the results are [a,1].
